title: Positive exact sparse spectrum learner
statement: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $n>0$, consider the deterministic query program on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube that charges the exact sparse spectrum rounding work, then runs the deterministic Goldreich–Levin learner with the corresponding exact sparse spectrum input and rounds its output to a sparse Fourier hypothesis in dimension $n$.
caveat: The construction uses the exact input, rounding-work, learner, and rounding maps, whose definitions are not supplied.
